parameters.content:
### 🧑‍🔬 Audit page: http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai4sg-audit
**Nothing to run here.** This workflow is the page's web server: it stays published, and every time someone opens the address n8n runs it once (reads the results, fills in `n8n/audit/audit.html`, returns the page). `?format=geo` returns the map boundaries (`n8n/audit/geo.json`, Natural Earth). Filtered-out sources are hidden by default.

### ✅ Pass / fail from the page
The page's **Pass** and **Fail** buttons post here (`/webhook/ai4sg-review`). Every decision is kept in the `reviews` table with the comment and reviewer name; the page shows the latest one.

parameters.query:
-- one row per source: analysed ones with their latest extraction, plus queued, filtered-out and not-downloaded sources
SELECT e.id, s.id AS source_id, e.fields, COALESCE(e.flags, '[]'::jsonb) AS flags, e.relevance_score,
       COALESCE(s.screen_relevance, e.confidence) AS screen_relevance, s.screen AS source_screen,
       CASE WHEN e.id IS NOT NULL THEN e.status WHEN s.status = 'passed' THEN 'queued' ELSE COALESCE(s.status, 'candidate') END AS status,
       COALESCE(e.created_at, s.created_at) AS created_at,
       s.url, s.title, s.title_en, s.why_relevant, s.country, s.language, s.source_type, s.format, s.search_engine, s.domain AS run_domain, s.domain_tags, s.pick,
       s.run_id, s.database, s.doi, s.relation, s.project_guess, s.files, s.text_chars, s.text_level, s.duplicate_of,
       par.id AS via_id, par.title AS via_title, par.url AS via_url,
       p.code AS project_code, p.name AS project_name, sp.method AS project_method, sp.reason AS project_reason,
       t.code AS tool_code, t.name AS tool_name,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM source_projects x WHERE x.project_id = sp.project_id) AS project_sources,
       rv.decision AS review_decision, rv.comment AS review_comment, rv.reviewer, rv.created_at AS reviewed_at
FROM sources s
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM extractions x WHERE x.source_id = s.id ORDER BY x.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) e ON true
LEFT JOIN sources par ON par.id = s.found_via
LEFT JOIN source_projects sp ON sp.source_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN ai_projects p ON p.id = sp.project_id
LEFT JOIN ai_tools t ON t.id = p.tool_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT decision, comment, reviewer, created_at FROM reviews r
                   WHERE r.extraction_id = e.id ORDER BY r.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) rv ON true
WHERE e.id IS NOT NULL OR s.status IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY COALESCE(e.created_at, s.created_at) DESC LIMIT 1500

SELECT id, started_at, finished_at, domain, counts, settings->>'Search engine' AS engine,
       settings->'Countries' AS countries, settings->>'Max sources to analyse in depth' AS max_sources
FROM runs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 30

-- the deployments (projects) with their tool and merged record (C3); experts review the sources (reviews), older project-level
-- decisions are still shown
SELECT p.id, p.code, p.name, p.aliases, p.implementing_org, p.countries, p.domain, p.synthesis, p.created_at, p.updated_at, p.deployment,
       t.code AS tool_code, t.name AS tool_name, t.developer AS tool_developer, t.aliases AS tool_aliases,
       (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(sp.source_id ORDER BY sp.source_id), '[]'::jsonb) FROM source_projects sp WHERE sp.project_id = p.id) AS source_ids,
       rv.decision AS review_decision, rv.comment AS review_comment, rv.reviewer, rv.created_at AS reviewed_at, rv.source_ids AS reviewed_sources
FROM ai_projects p
LEFT JOIN ai_tools t ON t.id = p.tool_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT decision, comment, reviewer, created_at, source_ids FROM project_reviews r
                   WHERE r.project_id = p.id ORDER BY r.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) rv ON true
ORDER BY p.updated_at DESC

-- a project decision records which sources the project had when it was reviewed
WITH pr AS (
  INSERT INTO project_reviews (project_id, decision, comment, reviewer, source_ids)
  SELECT p.id, $3, NULLIF($4, ''), NULLIF($5, ''),
         (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(sp.source_id ORDER BY sp.source_id), '[]'::jsonb) FROM source_projects sp WHERE sp.project_id = p.id)
  FROM ai_projects p WHERE p.id = $1 AND $1 > 0
  RETURNING project_id AS id, decision, comment, reviewer, created_at, source_ids
), er AS (
  INSERT INTO reviews (extraction_id, decision, comment, reviewer)
  SELECT id, $3, NULLIF($4, ''), NULLIF($5, '') FROM extractions WHERE id = $2 AND $1 = 0
  RETURNING extraction_id AS id, decision, comment, reviewer, created_at, NULL::jsonb AS source_ids
)
SELECT id, decision, comment, reviewer, created_at AS reviewed_at, source_ids FROM pr UNION ALL
SELECT id, decision, comment, reviewer, created_at, source_ids FROM er

parameters.content:
### 🔗 Project corrections from the page
On a source, **Not this project** gives it its own new project and **Move to P-…** links it to another project; on a project, **Merge into P-…** moves all its sources into the other project (its name becomes an alias). Posts to `/webhook/ai4sg-project`. Every project that changed is summarised again (C3); projects left without sources are removed.

parameters.query:
-- detach / move one source, or merge a project into another: the same database functions the website calls
SELECT code, name, project_ids FROM ai4sg_project_change($2, $1::bigint, $5, $3, $4)

-- (the function above removed deployments left empty) the deployments to summarise again
SELECT unnest($1::bigint[]) AS project_id

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify($('Save Project Change').first().json.code ? { ok: true, code: $('Save Project Change').first().json.code, name: $('Save Project Change').first().json.name } : { ok: false, error: 'project not found' }) }}

### 📄 Local copies
The page's *Local copies* links come here (`/webhook/ai4sg-file?id=<source>&name=<file>`): the file is read from the source library in the codex-runner container and passed through, so it opens even when the original site is down.

parameters.content:
### ▶ Analyse from the page
In *Not analysed yet* a reviewer can send any source (queued, set aside by the screen, or not downloaded) to the in-depth analysis. Posts to `/webhook/ai4sg-analyse` with the source ids (at most 30). A source without readable text is downloaded first; then **C2** extracts it (in the deployment the organiser placed it in, or linking it itself), and **③** re-summarises the deployments. The page is answered at once; results appear after a reload (about a minute per source).

parameters.query:
-- the chosen sources that have no in-depth analysis yet
SELECT id AS source_id, url, doi, COALESCE(files, '[]'::jsonb) AS files, COALESCE((domain_tags)[1], domain, '') AS domain,
       COALESCE(text_chars, 0) AS text_chars, false AS retry
FROM sources s WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[]) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM extractions e WHERE e.source_id = s.id)
ORDER BY id

-- a retried source that now has real text goes back to the screen; an extraction that was judged on a bot-check page
-- (and not reviewed yet) is dropped so the source is analysed again. A failed retry leaves the source as it was.
WITH old AS (SELECT id, status FROM sources WHERE id = $1),
dropped AS (
  DELETE FROM extractions e USING old
  WHERE $4::boolean AND $6::boolean AND e.source_id = old.id AND old.status = 'extracted' AND e.status = 'filtered_out'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.extraction_id = e.id)
  RETURNING e.id)
UPDATE sources s SET
  collect_tries = COALESCE(s.collect_tries, 0) + 1, collected_at = now(),
  files      = CASE WHEN $4::boolean OR NOT $6::boolean THEN $2::jsonb ELSE s.files END,
  text_chars = CASE WHEN $4::boolean OR NOT $6::boolean THEN $3::int ELSE s.text_chars END,
  text_level = CASE WHEN $4::boolean OR NOT $6::boolean THEN NULLIF($5, '') ELSE s.text_level END,
  status = CASE WHEN $4::boolean AND (old.status <> 'extracted' OR (SELECT count(*) FROM dropped) > 0
                                      OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM extractions e WHERE e.source_id = s.id)) THEN 'collected'
                WHEN NOT $6::boolean AND NOT $4::boolean THEN 'collect_failed'
                ELSE s.status END
FROM old WHERE s.id = old.id
RETURNING s.id AS source_id, s.status, s.text_chars

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Sources to Analyse').item.json.source_id, JSON.stringify($json.files || [{ url: $('Sources to Analyse').item.json.url, kind: 'main', error: $json.error?.message || $json.error || 'download failed' }]), $json.text_chars || 0, $json.ok === true, $json.text_level || '', $('Sources to Analyse').item.json.retry === true ] }}

parameters.content: **Re-screen** (`POST /webhook/ai4sg-rescreen` with `{domain, limit, min_relevance}`): screens again, with the current C1, the sources of a domain that were screened before the screen gave evidence types and domain tags (or whose screen failed). Sources already analysed keep their status and only get their domain tags.

parameters.query:
SELECT id AS source_id FROM sources s
WHERE s.domain IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULLIF($1, '') AND s.status NOT IN ('candidate', 'collect_failed')
  AND COALESCE(s.text_chars, 0) >= 300
  AND (s.screen IS NULL OR s.screen ? 'error' OR NOT s.screen ? 'evidence_type' OR NOT s.screen ? 'card'
       OR NOT (s.screen->'card') ? 'ai_method')
ORDER BY s.id LIMIT $2

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, sources: $('Sources to Rescreen').all().filter(i => i.json.source_id).length }) }}

parameters.content: **Organise** (`POST /webhook/ai4sg-select` with `{domain, max, analyse}`): runs the organiser of stage ② on the domain's queue (deployments, tools, duplicates and, with `max`, the selection). With `analyse: false` (default) it only records the grouping and which sources would be chosen and why (shown on the audit page); with `true` the chosen sources are analysed too. `max: 0` = no budget.

parameters.jsCode:
const b = $input.first().json.body || {};
return [{ json: { domain: String(b.domain || '').replace(/[^a-z_]/g, ''), max_sources: b.max === 0 || b.max === '0' ? 0 : Math.max(0, Number(b.max) || 10), dry_run: b.analyse === true ? 'false' : 'true', job_id: String(b.job_id || '') } }];

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, domain: $json.domain, max: $json.max_sources, analyse: $json.dry_run !== 'true' }) }}

parameters.content: **Project summaries** (`POST /webhook/ai4sg-resummarise` with `{project_ids, job_id}`): after a reviewer moves a source or merges projects on the website, C3 writes the summaries of the affected projects again.
